rv.q: At least two decades in the making, composer Duncan Sheik didn’t live to see this run of Nero, having died in hospital at the age of 56 in September 2026, and it naturally follows that this production is a tribute to him. Unfortunately, it fails to ‘mind the gap’ between tragedy and comedy, falling between the two.
Its biggest obstacle is discovering its own identity, as right now it veers between two completely different tones that don’t complement each other at all, instead resulting in an uneven watch.
Ultimately, Nero can’t decide whether it is a biting political satire, a psychological tragedy, a crude vaudeville comedy or a no-holds-barred rock musical.
Whatever the answer may be, it surely cannot be Nero: A New Musical.

cn.t: Despite a talented cast and some strong songs, this ambitious musical about the Roman Emperor falters with muddled storytelling and misplaced melodrama that undermines its political satire.
